content.rendered:
To Him who loved us and washed us from our sins in His own blood, and has made us kings and priests to His God and Father. Kings. Priests. Two crowns. One believer. This is the outcome of the cross for every one of us in Christ.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, August 4, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“To Him who loved us and washed us from our sins in His own blood, and has made us kings and priests to His God and Father, to Him be glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.”
Revelation 1:5-6 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

John opens the book of Revelation with a doxology to Jesus, the ruler of the kings of the earth. He names three things Jesus has done for the believer. He loved us. He washed us from our sins in His own blood. And He has made us kings and priests to His God and Father. Each verb builds on the previous one. The love came first. The washing came next. And the making-us-kings-and-priests is what the love and the washing produced.

The Passion Translation captures the movement beautifully: “He is the faithful witness from the dead, and the ruler over all the kings of the earth. Now to the one who constantly loves us and has loosed us from our sins by his own blood, and to the one who has made us to be a kingdom of priests to serve his God and Father—to him be glory and dominion throughout the eternity of eternities! Amen!” (Revelation 1:5-6 TPT). A kingdom of priests. That is the identity of the church.

The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “To Him Who ever loves us and has once [for all] loosed and freed us from our sins by His own blood, And formed us into a kingdom (a royal race), priests to His God and Father—to Him be the glory and the power and the majesty and the dominion throughout the ages and forever and ever. Amen (so be it)” (Revelation 1:5-6 AMPC).

Yesterday we saw Peter naming the church as a royal priesthood. Today John, in the opening of Revelation, confirms the same identity from a different angle. It is not just Peter’s language. It is heaven’s language. The King has made His people, through the shedding of His own blood, into kings and priests to God. This is not a metaphor stretched too far. This is the settled identity of every believer redeemed by the blood of Jesus.

The two callings are inseparable. As kings, we exercise dominion in the earth in the name of Jesus. We speak with authority. We enforce the victory of the cross. We push back the darkness. As priests, we minister to the Father. We worship. We intercede. We stand in the gap for others. We bring the offerings of praise and thanksgiving. The kingly authority is exercised through the priestly access. The priestly access flows out of the kingly identity. The two together are what the church was born to be.

For Gospelbuzz readers, this is the second Kingdom-identity truth of a two-day stretch. Yesterday, Peter. Today, John. Two apostles. One message. You are a king and a priest to God in Christ. Walk in that reality today. Do not shrink from the calling. The blood of Jesus is what made you this. Wear the crown well.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus has loved me, washed me from my sins in His own blood, and made me a king and a priest to You. I did not earn either identity. Both were purchased for me by the blood of the Lamb. As a king, I exercise dominion in Jesus’ name today. As a priest, I bring worship, intercession, and offerings to You. Both callings are mine because of what Jesus has done. To You be all glory and dominion forever and ever. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Jesus has made me a king and a priest to His God and Father. Both crowns are mine because of the blood of the Lamb. I walk in kingly dominion and priestly access today.

Go Deeper in the Word

  • Revelation 5:9-10 (NKJV): You have made us kings and priests, and we shall reign on the earth
  • 1 Peter 2:9 (NKJV): A royal priesthood, a holy nation
  • Hebrews 4:16 (NKJV): Come boldly to the throne of grace
